sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Himalayan is a government-linked solar-pump and EPC supplier entering a more substantial module-manufacturing phase, not an established high-utilization module compounder. At the NSE close of ₹81.90 on 19 October 2026, actual post-IPO shares imply ₹181.08 crore equity capitalization and 8.76x FY2026 reported earnings. The apparent cheapness is meaningful only if earnings turn into available cash. Three restated years produced ₹42.04 crore PAT but negative ₹3.69 crore cumulative CFO. [S1, S3, S4, S5]

The five-year base scenario produces ₹196.70 per share and 19.15% nominal annualized return, before investor taxes and trading costs, without new incremental credit beyond disclosed drawings and renewal of the existing cash-credit facility. It is a conditional calculation, not a prediction: closing receivable days improve from 269 in March 2026 to 150 by year five, supplier credit remains 60 material-cost days, and the proposed factory expansion is funded and commissioned. A 6x rather than 8x exit multiple reduces that return to 13.46%. A credible slower-collection bear needs ₹54.31 crore peak hypothetical additional credit and still produces a 73.61% price loss. Without that new credit, the bear is unfunded and has no valid investor IRR.

Final BQS is 4.98/10, GQS 5.00/10 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap, and IAS 3.00/10 after the funding-gate cap, versus raw IAS 5.845. Classification: speculative/funding-fragile; weak setup at this price, with High permanent-impairment risk and Medium evidence confidence. A separate no-growth, no-expansion, no-rescue test still produces a funding gap under credible collection and supplier-credit stress. The central question is collection and funding resilience, not whether a small solar company can report another year of accounting growth. No attractive-compounder designation is justified.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates & Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Himalayan Solar Limited, formerly Himalayan Solar Private Limited; NSE SME symbol HIMALAYAN; ISIN INE1B7I01014. Research cutoff is 20 October 2026, UTC; quote is the 19 October closing trade, not an executable bid. Listed 5 October 2026. Scope is standalone because the prospectus reports no subsidiaries; its statement of no “Group Companies” does not negate separately disclosed related-party relationships. Accounts use Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not an assumed Ind AS framework. Money is ₹ crore unless stated. The horizon is 20 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, in five investor-year blocks, not five financial years. The analytical equity hurdle is 15% nominal before personal taxes; it is not a WACC estimate. [S1, S3–S5]

G1 Integrity and minority protection: Conditional. Historical private-placement compliance orders and disclosed disputes warrant monitoring; the reviewed evidence does not establish material diversion, abusive RPTs or repeated serious minority harm. G2 Financial reliability: Conditional. Restated financials, opening liabilities and cash-flow arithmetic reconcile, but prior-period corrections, sharp receivable growth and a short comparable history limit confidence. Explained restatements are not treated as an automatic audit failure. G3 Funding and survival: Fail — evidenced in modeled credible no-rescue stress. A clean test cancels expansion, holds revenue and margin at FY2026 levels and assumes no AR loss or disputed legal cash payment. If inventory and supplier terms normalize to management's 30/30-day assumptions before collections improve, a ₹6.50 crore gap appears. Retaining longer supplier credit or thinner inventory can avoid that gap. This is a conditional stress assessment, not inevitable failure or evidence of actual company default. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Eleven observed listed sessions and the eligible SM series support a finite reference-position estimate; spreads, circuit exits and depth remain unverified. [S1, S3–S8]

Governance, growth decomposition, capital-return interpretation and valuation assumptions have Medium input confidence. The source values for the restated FY2024–FY2026 accounts, dated quote and issued shares have High retrieval/reconciliation confidence; the wider comparable history and liquidity implementation assessment remain Medium. Overall confidence is Medium, the weakest material conclusion area, not an average. Forecast uncertainty is High, especially around collections, project approvals and facility renewals. A precisely retrieved management estimate is not a verified future outcome.

sections.title: Scorecard & Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical primitive factors: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. IAS uses Q equal to the unrounded final BQS, R 8, D 3, P 5 and L 7. Each factor has positive and contrary evidence in the factor audit; no missing input is silently replaced by a neutral score.

BQS = 20%×4 + 20%×4 + 12%×8 + 10%×6 + 12%×6 + 10%×3 + 8%×5 + 8%×5 = 4.98. GQS raw = 40%×8 + 20%×6 + 15%×6 + 15%×6 + 10%×3 = 6.50. Persistent negative three-year CFO/PAT, rather than capex alone, activates the explicit CASH≤3 cap, so final GQS is 5.00. IAS raw = 25%×4.98 + 35%×8 + 20%×3 + 10%×5 + 10%×7 = 5.845; the explicit G3 funding-failure override caps final IAS at 3.00. Displayed half-up scores are 5.0, 5.0 and 3.0 respectively. Coverage is 100%; missing-factor bounds collapse to the raw scores. The GQS and IAS funding caps are the only composite overrides.

REV starts at 9 under the three-year CAGR rubric, but is capped at 8 because the relevant comparable evidence is shorter than five years and confidence is Medium. The small absolute starting revenue is not an extra penalty. R is mechanically 8 because the supported conditional base return exceeds the 15% hurdle by 4.153 percentage points. D is 3 because the linked bear creates both recapitalization risk and large shareholder loss. P is 5, not 8, because collection improvement and continued financing access still need to hold together. L starts at 9 from the observed turnover calculation and is explicitly reduced to 7 for the very short IPO-seasoned sample, lot-size constraint and unobserved spread/depth. There is no undisclosed composite haircut. These are research-policy heuristics, not statistically validated return predictors.

sections.title: Business Model & Economic Engine
sections.text:
FY2026 revenue was ₹166.1577 crore from design, manufacture, supply, installation and commissioning of solar products, ₹0.1854 crore from separately sold PV panels, and ₹4.0001 crore from skill training. Thus about 97.54% was the integrated solar-products/EPC activity, not standalone module sales. The economic engine is tender qualification, procurement, installation, acceptance and collection, with warranty/service obligations and bank guarantees. Panel capacity alone does not establish saleable output or cash earnings. [S1, business revenue tables]

Management reports more than 85,000 HP of solar-pump installations by FY2026. Tender experience, installation capability and relationships with implementing agencies help win work, but five customers accounted for 99.54% of FY2026 revenue. HAREDA alone was 50.00%, down from 85.15% in FY2025 and 88.48% in FY2024. The fall in the largest customer is genuine diversification within a still exceptionally concentrated customer base. Five suppliers supplied 90.20% of FY2026 purchases; dependence on externally purchased components and the absence of established exclusive procurement economics limit bargaining power. [S1]

Payment often follows milestone verification, invoice submission and retention release. The company attributes about ₹60 crore of FY2026 invoices to the final quarter and about ₹17 crore of receivables to retention. These explanations identify the collection mechanism; they do not prove recoverability or timing. Bank guarantees/letters of credit of ₹27.3473 crore are contingent exposures, not an additional funded-debt balance, but collateral and performance failure can consume liquidity. [S1]

sections.title: Moat, Industry & Competitive Position
sections.text:
The best moat argument is accumulated tender qualifications, project execution and service reach in solar pumps. The counterargument is stronger than a brand story: concentrated government purchasing, tender repricing, bought-in components and technology standards constrain pricing power. The old 40 MW polycrystalline line became commercially obsolete and stopped operating in August 2024; historical FY2024 production was only 9.02 MW, or 22.98% of the disclosed panel-unit capacity basis. A company exposed to that transition has not demonstrated a durable technology or low-cost manufacturing moat. MOAT 4 recognizes a working franchise, not a defensible industry leadership claim. [S1]

MNRE's scheme description confirms that subsidized agricultural pumps are administered through state implementing agencies and that portions of central assistance are released after project-completion and utilization documentation. This supports an accessible demand channel while explaining why acceptance and government-funding timing matter. The ministry page still states the original scheme period ending March 2026; no assumption of indefinite fresh sanctions is made. Search-index dashboard totals were inconsistent across portal pages and are not used as a company-addressable TAM forecast. [S9]

The prospectus's three useful but imperfect comparators are Ganesh Green Bharat, Solarium Green Energy and Australian Premium Solar. Its FY2026 comparison gives respective revenues of ₹1,064.27 crore, ₹368.15 crore and ₹707.96 crore, and EBITDA margins of 10.36%, 8.26% and 13.39%, versus Himalayan's reported KPI margin of 17.05%. Those are issuer-compiled peer figures, not independently re-audited comparable-company accounts. Mix and EBITDA definitions differ. They show that Himalayan's high margin should be tested, not automatically capitalized at a premium multiple; September peer prices are not current October valuation evidence. No verified market-share series was found. [S1, peer tables]

sections.title: Revenue Growth, Scale & Decomposition
sections.text:
Original audited FY2022 and FY2023 revenue was ₹41.49435 crore and ₹47.58586 crore. Restated FY2024–FY2026 revenue was ₹138.3192 crore, ₹142.4373 crore and ₹170.3432 crore. The FY2023-to-FY2026 three-year CAGR is 52.97%; the FY2024-to-FY2026 two-year CAGR is only 10.97%, with 2.98% growth in FY2025 and 19.59% in FY2026. Both windows matter. Five observations do not support a five-year CAGR, which requires six. No comparable interim cash-flow or full TTM series is invented. Original FY2023 PAT is not forced to match the different earlier-period base implied by prospectus ratios. [S1, S2]

The prospectus reports no material acquisition/merger/divestment in the previous ten years and no control change in the last five years. Growth therefore appears predominantly internally generated, but an exact volume/price/mix bridge is ND. It would be wrong to equate nominal revenue growth with physical module-volume growth: the company shifted from separately sold panels to integrated project delivery and training, while component prices and tender terms can move. The FY2024 step-up deserves more weight as a scale transition than as a recurring 50%-plus growth rate. [S1]

The 31 July 2026 unexecuted order table totals ₹140.2169 crore. Two July 2025 private-party 25 MW module LOIs contribute ₹95.04 crore, or 67.78%; other private orders add ₹14.176 crore. The table's private proportion is therefore 77.89%, while public work including training is ₹31.0009 crore and government-pump work about ₹27.6541 crore. The surrounding prose describes the book as mainly governmental, but the detailed classification does not support treating the whole total as firm government orders. The source itself calls the book unaudited and warns that orders may not convert into anticipated revenue or margin. This is a reconciliation of disclosed categories, not an allegation about the parties. [S1, printed 25–27 and 171–172]

An illustrative bottom-up decomposition preserves the model's base totals of ₹205/245/285/320/350 crore: EPC ₹186/211/236/256/270 crore, standalone modules ₹15/30/45/60/76 crore, and training ₹4 crore each year. At an assumed ₹15.2/W, terminal standalone module sales require 50 MW, or 31.25% of proposed 160 MW capacity. At ₹10/W, the same ₹76 crore needs 76 MW, or 47.5%. These are analyst utilization checks, not management forecasts or spot-price observations. The ₹15.2/W assumption is about 20% below the LOIs' headline ₹19.008/W implied value, whose tax/scope comparability is unverified. Modules embedded in EPC revenue are not counted again as standalone sales. Capacity can support the arithmetic; customer demand and realizations still need proof.

sections.title: Growth Quality, Reinvestment & Incremental Returns
sections.text:
The new 60 MW Mono-PERC facility's audited PPE note specifies commercial use on 20 March 2026. Another narrative gives March 2025; this analysis uses the audited note and preserves the inconsistency rather than claiming a full operating year of proven utilization. The proposed additional 100 MW project has an IPO allocation of ₹12.983 crore, with management targeting machinery order in October 2026, delivery in January 2027, installation/trials in February–March and commercial production in April 2027. Relevant testing/certifications are to be sought after trials, not assumed already obtained. [S1]

The capital-return measure deliberately counts operating working capital and restricted collateral. Invested capital is equity plus funded debt, less unrestricted cash and deferred-tax assets, with separately modeled current-tax, EPCG, accrued-interest and legacy-gratuity obligations added back so that their exclusion from operating WC does not create free financing. It is about ₹35.25 crore in FY2024, ₹55.34 crore in FY2025 and ₹85.28 crore in FY2026. Recast operating EBIT after noninterest bank charges, taxed at a common analytical 25.2%, produces average-capital ROIC of about 37.9% in FY2025 and 30.2% in FY2026. The two-year change-in-NOPAT/change-in-capital proxy is about 31.1%, above an explicitly assumed 12–16% nominal INR capital-cost comparison range. That range is not the 15% equity hurdle renamed as WACC. [S1; calculations]

These high proxies do not establish the new factory's project return. They combine a margin reset in the legacy EPC business with receivable investment, and the new line only entered use near year-end. The FY2024-to-FY2026 capital increase of about ₹50.03 crore includes ₹4.6851 crore net PPE growth and about ₹45.34 crore other operating capital. PPE reconciles from ₹6.4610 crore cash capex less ₹1.2371 crore depreciation and ₹0.5389 crore net-book disposals. No acquisition return is attributed. Three- and five-year comparable incremental-capital proxies are ND because the earlier audited basis is not reconciled to the restated capital series. CAP 6 reflects attractive accounting returns but unproven cash-realized returns on expansion.

Growth has not been self-funding: cumulative FY2024–FY2026 FCF proxy is negative ₹10.5598 crore before financing interest. The IPO is genuine new equity and reduces near-term pressure, but does not turn earlier receivables into cash. GQS is capped for persistent operating-cash weakness, not merely because growth capex is large.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The post-IPO promoter/group holding is about 70.13%. The prospectus states no pledged equity as of its date; that is not an independently confirmed perpetual absence of encumbrance. High ownership aligns economic exposure but also concentrates voting power. FY2026 remuneration for the three executive directors totaled ₹0.4130 crore, about 2.0% of PAT; all disclosed KMP remuneration totaled ₹0.6365 crore. Related-party loans, including ₹3.05 crore owed to Manjeet Singh at March 2026, are interest-free and repayable on demand. These are financing obligations, not permanent equity. Related rent and common-director entities are disclosed; the reviewed table does not substantiate an inference of material undisclosed sales or loans to promoters. [S1]

The original FY2023 report documents an auditor change; the 1 July 2026 peer-review report identifies Himanshu Mohta & Associates and explains re-audit for IPO eligibility. The restatement notes describe bonus/gratuity cutoff, audit fees, IPO-cost capitalization, interest gross-up, tax and receivable corrections. Original-to-restated PAT was ₹5.2047→₹4.9459 crore in FY2024, ₹15.1656→₹16.4306 crore in FY2025 and ₹21.1192→₹20.6662 crore in FY2026; the last differs by ₹0.0001 crore from the main P&L due to source rounding. These corrections weaken confidence in historical controls but are not, by themselves, a qualified opinion or proof of fabricated earnings. [S1, S2]

On 16 October 2026, the issuer disclosed two RoC orders dated 10 October concerning FY2015–2017 private placements: use of an ordinary bank account rather than a separate subscription account, and use of funds before allotment. Company penalties total ₹15 lakh (₹0.15 crore). Separate penalties on former directors are personal and are excluded from company obligations. The company says it voluntarily applied for adjudication on 2 April 2025 and expects no direct operational impact. Payment and final compliance closure were not verified. [S7]

The prospectus also discloses a pending criminal complaint, HVR Solar v Himalayan Solar and others, CT Cases/14548/2023, concerning a module-supply/payment dispute. Allegations remain unadjudicated; the source reports the petitioner-evidence stage and a 23 November 2026 hearing. A quality objection appears within the complaint narrative, but a complete independent company defence or subsequent court order was not reviewed. [S1, printed 291]

A GST matter follows a 28 June 2025 notice alleging input-tax credit based on fake invoices. The prospectus records the company's 24 July 2025 adjournment request and a 24 December 2025 assessment of ₹21.30128 lakh; it describes the matter as pending. This analysis does not independently establish the allegation or a later outcome. A consumer complaint concerning alleged non-installation of a pump seeks ₹3.81 lakh plus interest; the prospectus's August hearing date was explicitly not updated on the portal. Separate issuer litigation seeking ₹9.02376 lakh is not credited as recoverable cash. [S1, printed 292–293]

Execution is mixed: project revenue has scaled and the replacement line was installed, but the old line's obsolescence, dependence on a new ramp-up and delayed collections show that sales execution is not yet equivalent to cash execution. GOV 4 and EXEC 5 are proportionate judgments, not an integrity-failure finding.

sections.title: Financial Forensics & Per-Share Economics
sections.text:
The structured history retains five audited revenue/PAT observations, with original FY2022–FY2023 clearly separate from restated FY2024–FY2026. In the three comparable restated years, PAT was ₹4.9459/16.4306/20.6661 crore; CFO was negative ₹5.5246, positive ₹3.9030 and negative ₹2.0705 crore. Cash capex was ₹0.4067/4.4495/2.0115 crore. Cumulative CFO divided by cumulative PAT is negative 0.0878x, not an average of annual ratios. Capex explains additional FCF outflow, not the negative operating-cash realization itself. Reported CFO excludes interest classified in financing; the investor model separately pays that interest once. [S1]

Issuer KPI EBITDA was ₹7.8255/23.5750/29.0443 crore. Although its wording references finance cost, the table arithmetic adds back actual interest, not all bank/borrowing charges. Adding the remaining charges gives conventional EBITDA of ₹8.1493/24.0745/29.7888 crore. The model consistently uses the more conservative after-bank-charges cash-EBITDA definition. Operating margins on that basis rose from 5.66% to 16.55% to 17.05%; the change in profit cannot be described as revenue growth alone. The material-contribution proxy is not accounting gross profit because direct employee, installation and overhead costs remain below it. [S1]

FY2026 other income of ₹1.3497 crore includes ₹1.0511 crore insurance receipts and ₹0.2983 crore interest. Removing insurance at a common 25.2% tax yields normalized PAT of ₹19.8799 crore versus reported ₹20.6661 crore. The ₹0.4256 crore asset-disposal loss could separately be added back to reach ₹20.1982 crore, but that more favorable adjustment is not the core normalization. Export-obligation/custom-duty expenses are not removed merely because inconvenient. EBITDA valuation excludes deposit/insurance income; actual deposit interest is separately modeled with tax. [S1]

Receivables rose from ₹40.4516 crore in FY2024 to ₹66.3194 crore and ₹125.3374 crore, reaching 73.58% of annual sales. Closing DSO was approximately 107/170/269 days. Average-balance DSO, the standard turnover measure, was about 136.8 days in FY2025 and 205.3 in FY2026; these are not the same metric as management's closing-balance WC forecast. Receivables older than six months were ₹17.6784 crore versus ₹2.2525 crore in FY2025; more than one year old was ₹1.5547 crore, with no doubtful-debt allowance. Base and stress models therefore include explicit opening-AR impairments rather than assuming all recorded profit is cash. [S1]

FY2026 debt was ₹36.1239 crore, including cash credit ₹19.9601 crore, related-party ₹3.05 crore and current term maturities ₹4.0024 crore. Reported cash/bank balances of ₹10.3225 crore are not all available: ₹4.3671 crore fixed deposits are under lien and another ₹1.6531 crore is BG collateral outside the cash subtotal. Available cash is ₹5.9555 crore; total restricted collateral is ₹6.0202 crore. Net debt/after-bank-charge EBITDA is about 1.04x and operating EBIT/total finance cost about 10.35x. These coverage ratios are comforting on earnings but do not fund payment delays. [S1]

Every opening claim is assigned once. Ordinary WC includes receivables, inventory, supplier advances, government credits, operating security deposits, audit/employee/bonus/statutory/expense payables and customer advances. The ₹6.8234 crore income-tax liability is separately settled in the bridge; ₹3.0487 crore government credits remain a separate WC asset, not automatically a tax offset. EPCG ₹1.3459 crore is a dated cash claim. Accrued interest ₹0.0172 crore and current gratuity ₹0.0009 crore are paid once; noncurrent gratuity ₹0.0894 crore is retained/accreted, not all forced into immediate cash settlement. Noncurrent security-deposit liability ₹0.1706 crore and future tax accrual are deducted at exit. DTA is not free cash. [S1]

Bank-submitted stock/receivable statements differ from restated amounts in some earlier periods; the source explains provisional reporting and supplier-advance netting. For March 2026, reported bank payables ₹57.9060 crore versus net restated payables ₹58.1158 crore differ by ₹0.2098 crore. The ₹66.0670 crore gross payable less ₹7.9512 crore supplier advances reconciles the net figure. This is not treated as missing cash or concealment. [S1]

Actual issued shares increased from 1.6218899 crore to 2.2109699 crore through the fresh issue; the June 2025 bonus was not an economic capital inflow. At current shares, FY2026 pro-forma EPS is ₹9.3471, not the historical weighted-average ₹12.74. Fresh IPO gross cash is ₹60.67524 crore; OFS ₹7.3542 crore belongs to selling holders. Final net fresh proceeds are ₹52.7234 crore after stated ₹7.9519 crore expenses. Because ₹0.5034 crore of expenses had already been paid before March 2026, only ₹7.4485 crore is charged in the forward bridge; no double deduction is made. Minor ₹0.00006 crore prospectus rounding is retained. [S1, S3, S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The main method is an annual/monthly operating and cash model with a terminal EV/EBITDA bridge, not a current P/E extrapolation. All post-March financial balances are estimates except dated issued shares and disclosed debt utilization. The common bridge uses ₹195 crore revenue run-rate, 16% operating margin and closing DSO 255, pays legacy tax and interest, incorporates ₹4.902 crore disclosed post-March borrowing utilization, and keeps ₹1.59 crore undrawn Axis sanction out of actual cash. At entry, estimated general cash is ₹16.0613 crore, IPO-earmarked pools ₹41.8669 crore and debt ₹36.3271 crore. The bridge is not a reported October balance sheet. [S1, S3; analyst assumptions]

Base revenues are ₹205/245/285/320/350 crore and cash-EBITDA margins 15.5/15/14.5/14/13.5%. DSO improves to 220/190/170/160/150 days; inventory rises to 25 then 30 sales-days; supplier credit falls to 90 then 60 material-cost days. These are less optimistic on collections than management's 100-day assumption, but more generous on supplier credit than its 30 days. Project capex is 110% of ₹12.983 crore, with 0.8% of revenue maintenance capex. Tax is 25.2%, loan amortization and interest are scheduled monthly, existing cash credit renews, related-party principal is repaid in year one, and no dividend is added while cash is retained.

Bull revenue reaches ₹465 crore, margin 15.5%, DSO 100 days and exit 10x. Bear revenue reaches ₹225 crore, margin 9%, DSO 270 days, capex costs 120% with six-month delay and exit 6x; it includes 5% opening-AR impairment and identified tax/consumer stress payments. Severe revenue reaches ₹168 crore, margin 7%, DSO 330 days, capex costs 135% with twelve-month delay, 15% opening-AR impairment and no assumed new-credit rescue. Forecast margin, capex, debtor and creditor movements are linked to the same monthly cash and debt equations.

Base terminal equity is ₹378.00 crore EV plus ₹78.1221 crore excess general cash, less ₹20.0504 crore funded debt and ₹1.1690 crore retained legacy/tax claims, equaling ₹434.9027 crore or ₹196.70 per share. Restricted collateral, minimum operating cash and unused earmarked proceeds are not added. Bull gives ₹370.10 and 35.21% IRR. The conditionally funded bear gives ₹21.61 and negative 23.39% IRR; its ₹54.31 crore peak additional line is hypothetical, not sanctioned or guaranteed. Severe first breaches cash funding at 19 March 2027 and reaches a ₹73.21 crore peak gap: its price and IRR are NS. Terminal enterprise value is 86.9% of base common equity; much of the result depends on the terminal capitalization assumption.

Funding-failure alternatives are explicit. Without new credit, bear needs ₹40.75 crore and has no return calculation. A purely hypothetical equity rescue raises about ₹44.07 crore gross at ₹65.52, with 3% issue costs and dilution, and gives about negative 13.37% investor IRR; severe rescue raises about ₹77.54 crore at ₹49.14 and gives negative 36.55%. These are financing mechanics, not available offers. Existing cash-credit nonrenewal requires replacement funding even in the base. Keeping DSO at 269 days fails despite the modeled ₹40 crore new-credit ceiling; supplier credit compressed to 30 days requires ₹10.62 crore peak new credit and lowers base IRR to 17.84%. These checks prevent the headline return from masquerading as financing-independent.

The linked reverse model solves today's ₹81.90 price for a 15% return: terminal price ₹164.73. With the same margin trajectory, collection assumptions, 8x multiple and a full rerun of WC, capex, tax and debt, annual revenue of about ₹163.74/195.69/227.63/255.59/279.55 crore suffices. Terminal EBITDA is ₹37.74 crore. This is not an “easy hurdle”: slower growth also releases modeled WC and increases surplus cash, while the assumed collection reset and bank renewal remain essential.

The two-way sensitivity reruns all operating/tax/cash effects for a ±2 percentage-point shift in every annual margin and 6x/8x/10x exit multiples. At 11.5% terminal margin, IRRs are 8.90%/14.60%/19.34%; at 13.5%, 13.46%/19.15%/23.93%; at 15.5%, 17.38%/23.10%/27.93%. The full grid is funded under those collection assumptions. Base entry-price ceilings for 12%/15%/18% hurdles are ₹111.61/₹97.80/₹85.98. At 15%, the lower-margin 8x and base-margin 6x cases support only ₹80.48 and ₹76.55. These are assumption-dependent ranges, not observable fair values. Trading costs and market impact are not in headline IRR; explicit 1%, 2.5% and 5% per-side cost sensitivities accompany the model.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The single decisive failure variable is collections, including the availability of funding while collection is delayed. The strongest evidence against the favorable interpretation is that receivables nearly doubled in FY2026 while CFO was negative, despite a 17% operating margin. A low current P/E can be compensation for this rather than a market oversight. There is no independent evidence that the market has misunderstood the public figures.

The G3 test does not mechanically fail the company merely for funding discretionary growth. Its clean isolating case cancels the entire 100 MW expansion, leaves its ₹12.983 crore IPO allocation earmarked rather than using it as general cash, holds sales at FY2026 ₹170.3432 crore and operating EBITDA margin at its exact FY2026 level of about 17.05%, and retains actual FY2026 material, supplier-advance and government-credit ratios. There is no AR impairment or contingent GST/consumer payment. It retains 0.6% maintenance capex and all scheduled debt/known legacy obligations, calls related-party debt in month one, permits no new credit/equity and still renews existing cash credit at 9%.

In that clean test, actual closing DSO remains about 268.56 days (reported as 269). Inventory and supplier holding periods normalize to management's 30 sales-days and 30 material-cost days. The resulting ₹6.5031 crore cash gap starts on 19 September 2027. The source for all three holding periods is the prospectus's printed page 100/PDF 102; printed page 101/PDF 103 explains inventory normalization with restarted module production and shorter supplier credit in exchange for more competitive procurement. No top-line growth or new expansion is required for the test. The failure mechanism is inventory/supplier-credit normalization before collection improvement, not collapsed margins or assumed litigation loss.

Counterevidence is explicit: at the same high margin and no loss, 30 inventory days with 60 or 90 supplier days survives; 15 inventory days with 30 supplier days also survives. Retaining the actual approximately 7-day inventory ratio survives all three tested supplier terms. The cap is therefore a conditional stress assessment, not inevitable failure. It would be reassessed if the company demonstrates that lean inventory and longer supplier terms can persist, collections improve, or committed finance covers the timing mismatch.

A secondary stress holds sales flat or contracted, uses margins of 12/11/10/10/10%, inventory 15 days and 5% opening-AR impairment. The lower margins are analyst stresses, not issuer guidance: they fall in the broad 8.26–13.39% range of issuer-selected EPC/manufacturing peers, while historical Himalayan margins have varied widely. A 5% AR haircut is ₹6.2669 crore against ₹17.6784 crore of receivables older than six months; this is a sensitivity, not a finding that those receivables are bad. The clean test shows that neither assumption is necessary to produce a no-rescue gap under the management 30/30 working-capital structure. [S1, printed 100–101 and 110–112]

At 269-day collections and 90-day supplier credit this restrained business survives, important counterevidence. At the same 269-day collections and 60-day supplier credit it has a ₹4.11 crore gap, first in September 2027; at 285 days/60 days the gap is ₹11.58 crore. Contracting sales further to ₹155 crore still leaves a ₹1.12 crore gap at 285/60 days. A 60-day supplier stress is credible, though not a documented current demand, because management itself forecasts only 30 days; keeping FY2026's 269-day collections is not an unprecedented debtor shock. The funding gate therefore fails under the framework's no-assumed-rescue standard. An approved reallocation of unused capex proceeds, operating restructuring or new committed finance might cure particular gaps, but none is presumed. This is an analytical survival-test result, not a company default or insolvency allegation. [S1; linked calculations]

A linked failure path is fewer or slower government acceptances and unconverted private LOIs, followed by lower utilization, margin compression, slower debtor cash, shorter supplier credit and demand repayment or nonrenewal. Essential expenditure then requires expensive debt, discounted equity or contraction. The model's bear shows material impairment even if a lender funds it; severe/no-credit cases stop short of an invented recoverable shareholder value. Creditors and restricted-collateral beneficiaries have prior claims; common holders bear dilution and residual-value loss.

Recovery depends on documented acceptance/collections, retention release, bank renewal and an economically utilized approved line, not a quoted-price rebound. Quantified known company penalties and tax/consumer stress amounts are small beside the modeled WC gap, but disputed legal outcomes can also affect execution and confidence. Unquantified complaint exposure is not arbitrarily assigned a zero recovery assurance. High impairment risk distinguishes this from ordinary share-price volatility. [S1, S7]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
The base produces 2.40x terminal price and the bull 4.52x over five years, before any dividends; neither establishes a supported 5x or 10x outcome. Fivefold price growth over five years requires about 38.0% annualized appreciation; tenfold requires about 58.5%. A 5x/10x common-equity value at unchanged shares is ₹905.39/₹1,810.78 crore. Merely applying a manufacturing multiple to unutilized capacity cannot bridge that gap.

Revenue, margins, working capital, financing and per-share dilution would all need to support the outcome. A lower terminal multiple makes the requirement harder, while a rescue issue raises the equity hurdle further. The disclosed 160 MW capacity aspiration and private LOIs do not demonstrate that scale of cash-generative value creation. Classification: speculative/unsupported as a five-year multibagger thesis, not a probability-weighted target.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Use the nine structured monitoring items accompanying this report at each new result or relevant exchange filing. The priority sequence is collections and ageing, actual cash/claims, lender renewal, IPO deployment, factory commissioning/approvals, order conversion/customer mix, margin quality, legal closure and trading capacity. These are research review intervals, not scheduled alerts or portfolio instructions.

The most immediate evidence needs are actual post-IPO bank balances and deployment, reconciliation of the ₹6.8234 crore opening tax obligation and government credits, and acceptance/collection of the ₹60 crore late-year invoices. Watch whether cash improves because customers pay or merely because suppliers and lenders provide more funding. Monitor the existing ₹19.9601 crore cash-credit facility separately from new sanctioned-but-undrawn limits. [S1]

The factory's April 2027 commercial target is an alert point, not automatic proof of success: verify paid capex, approvals, yields, utilization and cash contribution. Two large LOIs should be traced to binding orders, deliveries, invoices and cash; a bigger headline order book is not enough. Score improvements require evidence of sustained execution and cash realization rather than a single favorable quarter.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Apply gates before the matrix: BQS 4.98, GQS 5.00 and funding-capped IAS 3.00 imply speculative/funding-fragile status and a weak setup at this price. The uncapped matrix would have indicated a speculative or mixed-quality watchlist at IAS 5.845, but it cannot override the failed no-rescue survival test. GQS 5.00 also fails the standard for a high-quality growth compounder. G1, G2 and G4 remain Conditional. G3 failure is not a finding of actual insolvency, fraud or suspension. Quality scores can be shown for descriptive comparison, but the name belongs in the funding-gate-excluded investment group rather than an ordinary investable ranking. The IAS reference position is an illustrative ₹5 lakh, not an allocation recommendation. Nearby decimal rankings should not be treated as economically precise.

The practical category is funding-resolution research watchlist, not a favorable new-purchase setup. At ₹81.90 the base clears the hurdle, but modest margin/multiple normalization can erase that spread, and the collection stress has a much larger financing consequence. A lower price alone can improve raw R/IAS but cannot remove the funding cap, repair negative cash conversion, renew a bank line or resolve a gate. Stronger BQS/GQS need sustained cash collection, cleaner working-capital discipline and demonstrated expansion returns.

For liquidity, the observed 5–19 October sample has eleven trading sessions, no observed zero-volume sessions and mean/median traded values of about ₹3.515/₹0.536 crore. Prelisting dates are not zero-filled into 20- or 60-session statistics. At the conservative ₹53.64 lakh daily value, a ₹5 lakh reference exit is 1.86 days at 5% participation, 4.66 at 2% and 0.93 at 10%; on the weakest observed day it is 14.35 days at 5%. A 1,200-share lot costs ₹98,280 at the quote, and five lots are ₹4,91,400. These are theoretical turnover capacities, not a suitable allocation or guaranteed exit. Promoter concentration leaves at most 29.87% nonpromoter holdings, not all readily available float. [S3–S6]

The 19 October NSE indicator file, effective for the next trading session on 21 October, carries the SME-not-regularly-traded caution. It does not establish actual default or misconduct. The eligible SM series and actual trades are more informative than inactive alternate-series rows; no universal surveillance clearance is inferred. Live spread, executable depth, circuit lock-ins and subsequent restrictions need checking before implementation. [S5, S6, S8]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The final 30 September 2026 prospectus is the principal financial/operating source, supplemented by the original FY2023 annual report, completed-allotment notice, official NSE daily trading and capital data, 16 October RoC disclosure and MNRE scheme description. The source ledger gives exact dates, locators, working URLs and read scope. Verified historical disclosure (V), reproducible calculation (C), management estimate (M) and analyst assumption (A) are kept separate. Original-report units are hundreds of rupees; prospectus financial tables are lakhs; both are converted explicitly to crore.

The main remaining gaps are actual October financial balances; precise tax-credit composition/recoverability; bank-renewal and covenant terms; order cancellation/acceptance terms and post-July conversion; new-line approval and mature-cohort economics; a complete price/volume bridge; later court/tax/penalty closure; independently normalized peer accounts; and live market execution. Targeted searches of major rating-agency domains did not locate a current Himalayan rating rationale. That is a search limitation, not proof that no rating exists. A monitoring-agency agreement is not a credit rating.

No unsupported acquisition, subsidiary, lease liability or minority interest is invented. Existing operating rent is retained in margins, with no lease capitalization/EBITDA mismatch under the disclosed AS basis. No unlocated warrants/options are inserted into current shares; any later issuance requires a new dilution model. Forecasts assume zero dividends, existing cash-credit renewal and ordinary operating continuity. The 15% hurdle is a research convention, not personalized financial advice. Assumptions should be replaced by actual filings as they become available; model reconciliation demonstrates internal consistency, not that the future will follow it.

restrained_survival_test.note: No rescue, no incremental credit, no discretionary 100 MW expansion, no release of dedicated IPO capex funds. The clean isolating grid holds sales, exact operating EBITDA margin, material ratio, supplier advances and government credits at FY2026 levels. It uses no AR loss or contingent legal payment, maintains actual closing DSO, renews existing CC at9%, retains maintenance at0.6% of sales and calls related-party debt in month1. Management's own30 inventory sales-days and30 supplier cost-days create a6.5031crore gap;30/60 or15/30 inventory/payable days survive. This is a delayed-collection stress, not a margin-collapse assumption. The secondary grid uses flat/contracted sales,15 inventory sales-days, maintenance0.6%, margins12/11/10/10/10%, 5% opening-AR impairment, statutory/legacy claims and all debt service. Secondary margins are stress assumptions below current17.05% but within the broad issuer-selected peer8.26–13.39% context;5%AR loss is6.2669crore versus17.6784crore older-than-six-month receivables, not an asserted bad-debt finding. Existing cash-credit renews; nonrenewal would worsen the test. DPO60 is a stress, not a documented current supplier demand: it is less severe than management's own30-day future forecast. DSO269 retains March2026 experience. DPO90 survival is contrary evidence. Failure is of this analytical no-rescue funding test, not actual company default. Approved reallocation of unused capex proceeds could change outcomes, but no such approval is assumed.

valuation.formula: EV = terminal EBITDA × exit multiple; equity = EV + surplus unrestricted cash − debt − retained claims; price = equity / diluted shares; IRR = (price/entry price)^(1/5) − 1 only if funded; dividends zero.
valuation.gate_result: G3 fails the credible no-growth/no-expansion/no-new-credit stress; this is not an actual-default finding. IAS capped at3.

Exact price/volume decomposition, independently normalized peers and current market share are ND. LOIs and company-estimated backlog are not guaranteed revenue.
New-line approvals, actual paid expansion costs, order conversion and post-July customer collections require subsequent evidence.
Later court/GST/penalty outcomes and a full independent issuer defence to the commercial complaint were not reviewed. Allegations remain allegations.
Only11 listed trading sessions exist at cutoff; prelisting dates are not zero trades. Live spread, depth, circuit exits and actual free float are not established.
Current credit-rating rationale was not located in targeted major-agency searches; absence of a search result is not proof of no rating.
